clue.text: Arrive at the position indicated in the middle of the page

definitions.text: Arrive at the position indicated in the middle of the page

parts.words: Arrive at the position indicated in the middle of the page
parts.note: the page's middle is pictured as a ranking slot, so arriving there means finishing as runner-up in a race

explanation.definitionFit: To finish a race behind only the winner is to be runner-up, the place a reader reaches halfway through a two-sided sheet.

clue.text: A hundred rushed around but were eventually restrained

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
rushed means hurried, or hastened

explanation.surface: A hundred people dashed about but were finally brought under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chastened has been subdued or humbled, made restrained by rebuke or hardship.

clue.text: Runner starts marathon in London, eagerly racing

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each following word in turn

explanation.surface: A runner sets off in the London Marathon, keen to race.
explanation.definitionFit: A miler is an athlete who specialises in running the one-mile race.

clue.text: Out, worthy cat? No, suffer quite the opposite

parts.note: the opposite of out is in
the opposite of a worthy cat is a worthless dog, a cur

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fine cat is out, then reverses everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite the opposite' tells us to flip each idea: out becomes IN, and a worthy cat becomes its contrary, an unworthy dog, CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and so suffer it.

clue.text: Ironstone employed as a neurotransmitter

indicators.note: employed suggests the letters of ironstone are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An iron-bearing rock is somehow used as a brain chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Serotonin is a chemical messenger that carries signals between nerve cells, affecting mood and sleep.

clue.text: Form a friend at school

parts.note: a form is a school class
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Advice to make a pal at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolfellow in the same class or year group is a pal from one's form.

clue.text: Anna omitted to include mention of being Ruth's mother-in-law

indicators.note: to include signals that the words Anna omitted hold the name within them

explanation.surface: Anna forgot to mention the Biblical in-law of Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, Ruth stays loyal to her widowed mother-in-law and goes with her to Bethlehem.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, Ruth's husband's mother is the widow who returns to Bethlehem with her.

clue.text: Dirty window pane often found in church

definitions.text: Dirty window pane often found in church

parts.note: dirty means soiled or stained
a window pane is made of glass

explanation.surface: A grimy pane is a common sight in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured windows depicting saints and scenes are a typical feature of churches.

clue.text: Swirling lasso without a tail

indicators.note: swirling suggests the remaining letters are spun into a new order
without means the letter A is taken away

parts.note: a lariat is a lasso

explanation.surface: A cowboy spins his rope that has no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes one A from LARIAT to leave LRIAT, and 'Swirling' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them, which is to trail them.

clue.text: Spices that he smuggles inside vehicles

annotationWithheld.why: Spices that he smuggles inside vehicles (9): CARS round DAMON, but no clue word gives DAMON ('that he' does not), and a search of the exact clue found nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: Spices that he smuggles inside vehicles

clue.text: Fishy captain is in form

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective pointing at a fish name; the answer is a snapper species

parts.note: a form is a school class, so school stands for form
the captain of a ship is its master

explanation.surface: A rather suspicious skipper is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The schoolmaster is a western Atlantic snapper, so 'Fishy' hints at the fish. 'in form' looks like 'on good form' but is the clue word for SCHOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a reef fish of the snapper family, so the word names something fishy.

clue.text: Bury before trouble starts to unfold

parts.note: to inter is to bury
pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: starts tells us to take only the opening letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: Get something buried before problems come to light.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold a meaning is to explain or construe it.

clue.text: Commonly named forger

definitions.meaning: the most common surname in Britain
a metalworker who forges iron at an anvil

explanation.surface: A forger with a very ordinary name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the commonest English surname, and a blacksmith is a craftsman who forges metal.

clue.text: Roaming in Devon, he ended up in the Netherlands!

definitions.text: Roaming in Devon, he ended up in the Netherlands!

indicators.note: roaming suggests the letters wander into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man wandering in an English county somehow finds himself in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its letters with IN and HE rearrange into a Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a city in the southern Netherlands, home of the electronics firm Philips.

clue.text: Piles of grass chimneys

parts.note: hay is cut and dried grass
chimneys are also called stacks

explanation.surface: Heaps of grass become chimneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Large heaped mounds of dried fodder stand in fields after mowing.

clue.text: Uncoiled viper aims to play the bloodsucker

indicators.note: uncoiled suggests the snake's letters unwind into a different shape

explanation.surface: A snake unwinds intending to act like a blood-drinking creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To vampirise someone is to prey on them like a vampire, drinking their blood.

clue.text: A soggy old grub

parts.note: soggy means wet

explanation.surface: A damp, stale meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, but it means a larva: the aweto is a New Zealand caterpillar.
explanation.definitionFit: The aweto is a New Zealand caterpillar, a larva often infested by a fungus.

clue.text: Exit scene to regain ones livelihood

indicators.note: regain hints at the letters of exit scene being gathered back up in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An actor leaves the stage to recover their means of living.
explanation.definitionFit: One's existence can mean one's means of subsistence or way of living.

clue.text: Even again, daddy's light-headed

indicators.note: even means take the letters in even positions, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Equal once more, Dad feels dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling dizzy or faint is being light-headed.

clue.text: Characteristic behaviour is masculine

parts.note: behaviour means manner
M is the abbreviation for masculine in grammar

explanation.surface: A man's typical conduct is manly.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannerism is a habitual gesture or trait, a characteristic of a person.

clue.text: The beer on the right is active

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: The beer on the right is lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wide awake and lively is being on the ball, quick to respond.

clue.text: Steer clear of lady now in

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, is a lady
AD, the present era, means now

explanation.surface: Avoid the woman who is at home.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno Domini) labels the current era, so it can stand for now.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to avoid or dodge it.

clue.text: Shows that registers include a central tritone

indicators.note: include tells us the list word holds other letters within it

parts.note: indices are registers or lists

indicators.note: central tells us to take the middle letter of the word tritone

explanation.surface: A musician points out that the scales contain a dissonant interval.
explanation.walkthrough: A tritone is a dissonant musical interval of three whole tones; its middle letter is T.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to point it out or show it.

clue.text: Fed up with the study I'd turned upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upside down means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a study
I'd is written as ID

explanation.surface: Fed up with his study, he turned it upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned upside down' flips DENID, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dined is to have eaten a meal, so one has been fed.

clue.text: Crikey! Soldier has short legs, for example

definitions.text: Crikey! Soldier has short legs, for example

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like crikey
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a short-legged soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh corgi is a dog breed famous for its very short legs.

clue.text: Support for laurel's Chinese charge

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A Chinese charge for the support of laurel bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar used as a prop.

clue.text: Classify alien without a special translator

indicators.note: without means some letters are taken away

parts.note: a stranger is an alien

explanation.surface: Categorise a foreigner without a special interpreter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the S, the T and the final R from STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To range things is to arrange or class them in order.

clue.text: Selena whined about such publicity

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of Selena whined are moved around

explanation.surface: A celebrity complained about the press attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner line in a newspaper is a form of press publicity.
